adversarial_test_results.prompt: Mara kept a field journal through every leg of the northern survey, and the entries grew longer as the weeks passed. On the first morning the team left the harbor town before sunrise, their packs heavy with dried fish, wool blankets, brass compasses, and folded paper maps. The road climbed through pine forest where meltwater crossed the ruts, and the porters sang low work songs to keep their pace steady on the grade. By midday they reached a stone bridge over a fast river, and Mara sketched its single arch while the cook boiled tea on a driftwood fire. The second day brought fog so thick the lead guide walked with a bell, and the mules refused the higher trail until the sun thinned the mist near noon. They camped beside a shepherds hut whose owners shared barley soup, hard cheese, and news of a rockslide blocking the eastern pass. Mara mended a torn strap, dried her socks over the coals, and copied star fixes into the margin of her chart. On the third day the party crossed an alpine meadow loud with marmots, then descended a scree slope one step at a time with ropes tied between pairs. A thunderstorm forced them under an overhang where they waited two hours, watching hail bounce off the stones and listening to the river rise below. The fourth morning dawned clear and bitterly cold, and frost silvered the tent seams before the sun cleared the ridge. They rationed the last of the coffee, traded spare batteries for fresh bread at a wayside cabin, and marked three new cairns along the watershed trail. A lame mule slowed the column, so Mara redistributed its load among the stronger animals and logged the change in her inventory table. On the fifth evening the valley finally opened beneath them, lamplit villages strung along the water like beads on a string. The team picketed the animals, hung their wet clothes on lines strung between poles, and ate the remaining stew in companionable silence. At the final campsite, the guide raised her lantern against the dark and softly whispered, We rest here.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Long-context holdout placing a novel reported-speech verb completion deep inside a multi-hundred-word coherent travelogue, testing that the local ramp survives far from the document start.
